title: LandlordGuard Loyalty Renewal Cap for Long, Quiet Records
content:
**Rule.** The renewal cap percentage on the LandlordGuard Dwelling Fire Policy rewards a long, quiet record on the building. A policy whose original effective date is at least 60 whole months before the upcoming effective date and that has no claim reported with a loss date in the tier's claims lookback (36 calendar months on every tier) up to today takes 5 points off the tier's renewal rate cap; a policy insured at least 60 whole months with exactly one such claim takes 2 points off; any other policy keeps the tier's renewal rate cap.

The renewal cap percentage is the percentage by which the expiring term premium is increased to give the capped figure of the renewal term premium.

## Truth table

| Whole months from the original effective date to the upcoming effective date | Claims with a loss date in the 36 calendar months up to today | Renewal cap percentage |
|---|---|---|
| 60 or more | none | the tier's renewal rate cap less 5 points |
| 60 or more | exactly 1 | the tier's renewal rate cap less 2 points |
| 60 or more | 2 or more | the tier's renewal rate cap |
| fewer than 60 | any number | the tier's renewal rate cap |

## Resulting caps by tier (percent)

| Tier | Tier's renewal rate cap | 60+ months, no claim | 60+ months, one claim | Any other policy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-1 Basic | 25 | 20 | 23 | 25 |
| DP-2 Broad | 20 | 15 | 18 | 20 |
| DP-3 Special | 15 | 10 | 13 | 15 |
| DP-3 Special Plus | 15 | 10 | 13 | 15 |
| DP-3 Premier | 12 | 7 | 10 | 12 |
| DP-3 Portfolio | 10 | 5 | 8 | 10 |

## The tenure test on both sides (hypothetical dates)

The upcoming effective date is the first day of the renewal term, the expiration date of the term now in force. With an upcoming effective date of 1 July 2025, an original effective date of 1 July 2020 gives 60 whole months and meets the test; 2 July 2020 gives 59 whole months and does not.
